name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,600

clue.text: I am one to tolerate drug-taking naked king

indicators.note: to take something in is to receive it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: naked means bare
E is ecstasy, the usual crossword drug
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A long-suffering confession: someone puts up with a stoned, unclothed monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: BARE takes in E, then R follows. The definition is the whole 'I am one to tolerate' phrase, as if the answer were speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts up with things bears them, so they are a bearer, the agent noun of bear.

clue.text: Airs shown by a daughter during posh formal dances

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits within its span of time

blocks.note: grand formal dances are balls
taken as written
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Tunes being sung by somebody's daughter at a society ball.
explanation.walkthrough: A and D go together inside BALLS, between the L and the S.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or song, and ballads are songs telling a story, so they are examples of airs.

clue.text: German dons behind blue atmospheric phenomenon

indicators.note: to don is to put on clothing, so the outer pieces are worn around the letter

blocks.note: behind in time means after
G is the abbreviation for German
feeling blue is feeling low

explanation.surface: A German putting on blue clothes, apparently at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' reads as university teachers, but here it is the verb meaning puts on, with the German letter worn by the two words around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The glow left in the sky after sunset is a recognised optical effect of the atmosphere, so it qualifies as a phenomenon.

clue.text: He is one not lacking bit of nous, but simple

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is taken out
a bit is a small piece, here just the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium, which is an element
nary is a dialect word for not one, as in nary a word
first letter of nous

explanation.surface: A man described as not short of common sense, yet simple-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a man, but it is the symbol for helium. NARY loses its N, leaving ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic or straightforward, so it is a direct synonym of simple, as in elementary arithmetic.

clue.text: Hoskins must wear contraceptive covering, being hot stuff!

indicators.note: whatever is worn is surrounded by the clothing, so a letter sits inside

blocks.note: a cap is a contraceptive diaphragm
the setter, Hoskins, refers to himself as I
scum is a film covering the surface of a liquid

explanation.surface: The setter cheekily announces he must use protection because he is so hot.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for I, which goes inside SCUM after CAP. Hoskins is known for risqué surfaces like this.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsicums include chilli peppers, which are fiery to eat, so they are literally hot food.

clue.text: Missionary position is used in Antilles regularly

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept
something used in a thing is put inside it

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters
POS is the abbreviation for position

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark that the missionary position is popular in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missionary position' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops after 'Missionary'. The Antilles are Caribbean islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were the first Christian missionaries, sent out to spread the faith, so the word names a missionary.

clue.text: Lose your rag as rubbish son needs to get up

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up means rising from bottom to top, so the order flips

blocks.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, to rubbish
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent losing their temper because a lazy son won't get out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' looks like an adjective describing the son, but it is a verb meaning criticise. 'Lose your rag' is British for losing your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to speak or act suddenly in anger, which is exactly what losing one's temper involves.

clue.text: One heading to nightclub to tuck into brew or a Bud

indicators.note: a heading sits at the top, so only the opening letter is wanted
to tuck into is to be pushed inside something

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
first letter of nightclub
cha is slang for tea, a brew

explanation.surface: Someone off to a nightclub, choosing between a cup of tea and a Budweiser.
explanation.walkthrough: Bud looks like the beer brand, but it means a pal. China means mate in Cockney rhyming slang, from 'china plate'.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang china plate rhymes with mate, so china is a friend, the same as a bud or buddy.

clue.text: Hills soldiers and devout duke climbed close to Leeds

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing goes from the bottom upwards, so the order turns round
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter counts

blocks.note: soldiers are men in crossword shorthand
pi is short for pious, devout
D is the abbreviation for duke
last letter of Leeds

explanation.surface: Troops and a religious nobleman hiking up hills near Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets the hills near Leeds, but they are in Somerset in south-west England; Leeds only provides its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mendips are a range of limestone uplands in Somerset, so the plural proper name refers to a group of hills.

clue.text: Line of speed

blocks.note: first meaning: a line of work, a profession
second meaning: to rush along fast and out of control

explanation.walkthrough: 'Line of speed' reads like a racing line or speed trap; split it into two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for someone's working life and a verb for hurtling along headlong, as a car careers down a hill.

clue.text: In Paris, bed group of soldiers in unit

blocks.note: lit is French for bed
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Soldiers billeted in Paris, bedding down together in their unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit' looks military, chiming with the soldiers, but it is a unit of measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric measure of volume, so it is one of the standard units of measurement.

clue.text: Song and dance singer recalled chart success in Love

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: a song and dance is a fuss, an ado
an informer sings to the police, and an informer is a rat
a number one, No 1, is the top chart success

explanation.surface: A song-and-dance performer looking back fondly on a hit record called Love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' suggests a vocalist, but it is an informer who sings to the police. No 1 is written NOI and read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep, worshipful affection, so it is a strong synonym for love as a noun.

clue.text: Possibly treaties meet with anger, rioting and touch of sadness

indicators.note: rioting is wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement
a touch is a small trace, here just the first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
first letter of sadness

explanation.surface: Peace treaties provoking angry riots and a little sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks treaties as one example of the answer, the reverse of the usual definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Treaties are formal pacts between states, so they are one kind of the broader category of agreements.

clue.text: One little doggy running around island

indicators.note: running around means turning back on itself, so the order is flipped

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
a lab is a Labrador, shortened, hence little

explanation.surface: A small dog racing round and round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' does not mean a small dog: it says the dog's name is shortened, Labrador to lab.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian tourist destination east of Java, a single island in the archipelago.

clue.text: Man on Later playing purely to show off?

indicators.note: playing about with something means messing it around into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician appearing on the TV show Later just to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: Later... with Jools Holland is a BBC live music show, so 'playing' seems to mean performing music.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ornamental is decorative, serving for display rather than for any practical function.

clue.text: Sailor seen with Her Maj grabbing posh bloke giving the fingers?

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so one piece is clasped inside the other

blocks.note: an old salt is a sailor
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
U means upper class

explanation.surface: A sailor beside the Queen, caught grabbing a toff who is making a rude gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: SALT plus ER take in U. 'Her Maj' is a British slang shortening of Her Majesty.
explanation.definitionFit: A saluter touches the fingers to the brow in respect, a cheeky take on rude finger gestures, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Van Gogh was halfway to being this brave, having lost head

definitions.text: Van Gogh was halfway to being this

indicators.note: losing a head means the top letter is cut away

blocks.note: brave means unafraid

explanation.surface: A comment that Van Gogh was half-courageous, or rather lost his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: Van Gogh famously cut off one ear, so with one of two gone he was halfway to having none.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking ears entirely, the painter after mutilating himself had lost half of them, a witty factual description.

clue.text: Discharge English soldier that's hit volunteers from the south

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the south means from the bottom up, backwards

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a soldier is a man in the ranks
a hit record is a No 1
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An English soldier wounded and dismissed from the army, along with southern volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' suggests sending a soldier home, but it is a noun for something given off.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something that flows out from a source, such as a gas or light, so it is a discharge.

clue.text: Turn on debtor that's ready for it after bit of petting

indicators.note: a bit is a small piece, here just the first letter

blocks.note: first letter of petting
a debtor is one who owes, an ower
up for it means ready and willing

explanation.surface: A saucy scene: someone aroused and keen after a little petting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn on' suggests arousal, chiming with the petting, but it means switching on a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: To power up a device is to switch it on, supplying electricity so that it starts working.

clue.text: Saucy sort of advance leads to absolutely torrid affair

definitions.note: adjective standing for a noun, read as 'sauce type'

indicators.note: leading letters are the ones in front, so first letters are kept

blocks.note: making a pass is a romantic advance
first letters of each word

explanation.surface: A cheeky flirtatious approach that ends in a steamy fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' looks like it means risqué, matching the surface, but it points at a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Passata is sieved tomato purée used as a base for Italian cooking sauces, making it a saucy ingredient.

clue.text: Artist involved in track by America or Bread

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up within it

blocks.note: a track is a path
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
A is an abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A musician guesting on a song by the bands America or Bread.
explanation.walkthrough: America and Bread were both 1970s soft-rock bands, so 'track' looks like a song and 'Bread' a group's name. 'or' does no work beyond joining.
explanation.definitionFit: A paratha is a flaky, layered flatbread from South Asian cuisine, so it is a kind of bread.

clue.text: Daily forced to ditch front cover in farcical event

indicators.note: a front cover is the very first thing, and ditching it drops the opening letter

blocks.note: a daily is a cleaning lady, also called a char or charwoman
made to do something is forced to do it

explanation.surface: A daily newspaper made to drop its front page in a ridiculous episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper, but it is British slang for a cleaner who comes every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, an obviously false show put on for appearances, which is a farce.

clue.text: Is it possible that a half-cut European is a state?

indicators.note: cut in half means only one half survives

blocks.note: can asks whether something is possible
taken as written
a Dane is a European from Denmark

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether a tipsy European could be in a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk and 'a state' suggests being in a mess, but it means a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a sovereign country in North America, and a state can mean any independent nation.

clue.text: Peak time's ending! Vacation at front with English break?

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter
the front of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: last letter of time
first letter of vacation
E is the abbreviation for English
a rest is a break

explanation.surface: Peak holiday season is over, and someone hopes for an English getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peak time' reads as a phrase meaning the busy season, but 'Peak' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's highest mountain, in the Himalayas, so it is the best-known peak of all.

clue.text: Ultimately defines actor as one acting other than they are

definitions.text: one acting other than they are

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: last letter of defines
a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: A definition of an actor as someone pretending to be someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a dictionary entry for actor, but 'defines' only gives its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is an impostor or fraud, a person pretending to be something they are not.

clue.text: Okay by the cops to bump off leading liberal? That's terrible!

indicators.note: to bump off is to kill, so a letter is removed
the leading letter is the one at the front

blocks.note: acceptable to the police means within the law
first letter of liberal

explanation.surface: Outrage at police apparently sanctioning the killing of a prominent Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading liberal' suggests a politician, but it is just the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful means very bad or dreadful, a direct synonym of terrible as an adjective.

clue.text: Dander gets up with game woman who's really dominant

indicators.note: to get something up is to rig or arrange it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A formidable, game woman whose temper is easily roused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets up' sits naturally after 'Dander', from the idiom 'get your dander up', meaning to get angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A grande dame is an imposing older woman of influence in her field, someone who dominates by stature.

clue.text: Palliative primarily given to sick?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: first letter of palliative
sick means ill

explanation.surface: Pain relief being handed to someone who is unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the question mark flags that the entire sentence describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tablets are the commonest form in which soothing medicine is handed to patients who are unwell.

clue.text: Bad face lift gets foremost of doctors distressed

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so the letters are botched into a new order
foremost means at the very front, so only the first letter counts

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of doctors

explanation.surface: A botched cosmetic operation upsets the surgeons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad face lift' reads as a cosmetic disaster, but 'Bad' signals rearranging the face lift letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Afflicted means troubled or suffering, so it is a synonym of distressed as an adjective.

clue.text: Flatulent? In the end, booze can give you wind

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word

blocks.note: last letter of flatulent
wine is booze

explanation.surface: A warning that drinking too much will leave you gassy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like flatulence, the noun, but it is the verb, rhyming with find.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine is to wrap or coil something around, as ivy twines round a post, the same as wind.

clue.text: A couple of lines with Large Earl in motor and things are ok!

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
L is line, so two lines are LL
a motor is a car
L is the abbreviation for large
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A man called Large Earl snorting cocaine in his car and declaring all is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' suggests cocaine, but each line is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: The all-clear is the signal that danger has passed, so it announces that everything is safe.

clue.text: Fighter, perhaps with bit of tan and heavenly body

indicators.note: a bit is a small piece, here just the opening letter

blocks.note: a fighter is a type of military aircraft
first letter of tan

explanation.surface: A boxer with a bit of a tan and a gorgeous physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' suggests a boxer and 'heavenly body' a stunning figure, but they are an aircraft and an object in space.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet is a large astronomical object orbiting a star, one of the bodies in the heavens.
